title: 40 Free Infographic Templates That Look Professionally Designed
excerpt: 40 free infographic templates you can customize today, from Canva-ready layouts to fully editable designs that don't look like everyone else's slide deck.
html:
Free infographic templates have a reputation problem: most of them look free. Cramped layouts, clashing colors, and clip-art icons that immediately signal "non-designer." But when you need to turn a complex process or a list of statistics into a visual asset in under two hours, building from scratch isn't an option. This collection of 40 free editable templates across the main infographic styles — statistical, process, timeline, comparison, and lists — was curated to solve this. Each one enforces correct spacing, clean typography, and a modern color palette so you can focus on your content without looking like you used a default template.

Why Most Free Templates Fail (And How to Spot a Good One)

The internet is full of "free infographic maker" sites, but most of their templates suffer from three design flaws that undermine your credibility:

1. Cluttered grids. Amateur templates try to fill every pixel with shapes, lines, or decorative icons. A good template uses white space as a design element, giving your eyes room to breathe between data points.

2. Too many fonts. A professional infographic uses two typefaces maximum — one for titles, one for body copy. Templates that mix four or five fonts immediately look chaotic and amateurish.

3. Inconsistent icons. Using a hand-drawn line icon in one section and a flat, filled-color icon in another breaks the visual rhythm. The best templates use one cohesive icon family throughout the design.

When browsing templates, look for structure first, style second. Swap the colors and fonts to match your brand; what you can't easily change is a bad layout grid.

The 40 Templates, Grouped by Style

This curated library includes templates built for the major design platforms — Canva, Figma, and PowerPoint:

* Statistical Infographics — 10 templates featuring large KPI callouts, pie charts, and grouped bar layouts. Best for survey results, annual reports, and industry stats.

* Process & How-To Guides — 8 templates with linear flows, flowcharts, and cyclical process loops. Enforces a clear reading order with numbered steps and arrow connectors.

* Timelines & Milestones — 8 templates using horizontal and vertical time axes. Ideal for company history, project roadmaps, and historical event tracking.

* Comparison & Versus — 6 templates featuring side-by-side columns and versus layouts. Clean division grids ensure attributes match up at the same optical height.

* List & Informational — 8 layouts built for social sharing. Low complexity, typography-forward designs that turn article summaries into visual content.

All 40 are free to download and edit on IllustrateWords, with no sign-up or watermarks required.

How to Customize Without Breaking the Layout

The fastest way to ruin a template is to dump your raw text into it without editing. Templates are designed for specific word counts. If a block has room for 15 words and you paste 50, the text overflows, the margins break, and the clean design disappears.

To customize successfully, edit your copy to fit the template's placeholders. Keep headers under five words, body copy under 20 words per section, and let the charts or icons do the heavy communicative work.

In Canva, use the "position" panel to align elements to the center or sides rather than dragging them by eye. In Figma, keep auto-layout active so the template adjusts its boundaries automatically as you edit. If a chart isn't matching your data exactly, build it in Datawrapper first, export it as an SVG, and drop it into your design tool.

One final rule: swap placeholder icons for symbols that actually match your content. If your step is about "launching a campaign," don't use a default lightbulb icon — find a rocket or a megaphone that supports the verb.

A professional infographic is a balance of content, layout, and restraint. Use these 40 free infographic templates to skip the layout phase and start customizing with confidence. See our Chart Types Guide for help selecting the right visualization format before you fill in your template.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where can I find free infographic templates?

The best sources for free editable templates in 2026 are: Canva's template library (excellent for beginners), Figma Community (best for custom control and design teams), and the curated Examples Gallery on IllustrateWords. All templates in our gallery are free to download and edit across platforms, with no attribution required.

Can I edit these templates in Canva?

Yes — most of the templates in this collection are fully compatible with Canva's free tier. Click the template link, select "Use template for design," and you can edit text, swap colors, and upload your own brand assets immediately in your browser.

How do I make a template match my brand?

Update three elements: the color palette, the typography, and the icon style. Swap the template's primary colors for your brand's main colors, change the font selection to your brand's typefaces (no more than two), and ensure all icons match your brand's visual style (outline vs filled).

What software is best for editing infographic templates?

Canva is the best choice for most marketers and non-designers because of its drag-and-drop simplicity and built-in library. Figma is preferred by design teams who need precision, version control, and custom grid systems. PowerPoint works well for presentation-embedded templates.

How do I export my finished infographic?

Export as a PNG for social media, email embeds, and blog posts to keep colors bright and file sizes manageable. Export as an SVG if you are embedding the infographic on a website and want it to stay sharp at any screen resolution. Export as a PDF for printing.
